### J-1 Drafter writes a decision record directly
- quote: "record it as a decision with `@nio:remember`, so the tasks jury can see it."
- quote: "one new decision record under `.nio/memory` naming the choice and the spec's slug"
- situation (consistency): the tasks drafter is an agent and it makes a design choice. FR-22 and AC-7 have it write a decision record under `.nio/memory` directly. D-261024-kljr (current) says only the configured memory writer writes `.nio/memory/`, other agents append candidates to `promote.md`, and "New pipeline stages ... never write records themselves." No change request exists against kljr. The drafter's choice should instead be a candidate in the run's `promote.md`, which the writer promotes, or the spec needs a change request against kljr first.
- situation (consistency): the tasks drafter is an agent, not the configured memory writer. Under D-261024-kljr (current, in the pack) only the memory writer writes `.nio/memory/`, and other agents append candidates to the run's `promote.md`. The remember skill says a non-writer "may only add candidates". FR-22 and AC-7 require the drafter to write a decision record itself, and the spec carries no change request against D-261024-kljr. A drafter that follows FR-22 breaks the single-writer rule the memory was built on.
- situation (consistency): D-261024-kljr (current) says "Only the configured memory-writer role writes `.nio/memory/`. Other agents append candidates to the run's `promote.md`", and its Reuse section says "New pipeline stages emit an event and append candidates; they never write records themselves." The tasks stage is a new pipeline stage. When the drafter makes a design choice, FR-22 has it write a decision record directly, which skips the writer's admission rule and dedup. The spec does not cite D-261024-kljr and no change request against it is in the pack, so the requirement goes against a current decision without the change request the memory rules require.
- fix: have FR-22 and AC-7 require a candidate in `.nio/runs/<run>/promote.md`, promoted by the memory writer. Or write a change request against D-261024-kljr before the spec proceeds.
- validation: confirmed: D-261024-kljr (status human, in /home/work/nio/.nio/memory/sync/) says only the configured writer writes `.nio/memory/`, and new stages "never write records themselves". skills/remember/SKILL.md lines 23-24 say a non-writer "may only add candidates". FR-22 and AC-7 ask the tasks agent for a record under `.nio/memory`, and no change request against kljr exists.
- disposition: spec-fix by agent: FR-22/AC-7: drafter appends a decision candidate to promote.md and names the choice in tasks.md; the memory writer records it (follows D-261024-kljr, which is in force)

### J-2 Tier values described as already shared with agent cards
- quote: "the same values agent cards use."
- situation (consistency): FR-15 says the task tier values `cheap|strong|max|frontier` are "the same values agent cards use". `src/nio/agents.py` line 12 has `TIERS = {"cheap", "strong", "max"}`, and `nio agents` rejects any other tier. Until FR-17 lands, a card with `tier: frontier` fails validation, so the two sets do not match yet. Either say FR-15 depends on FR-17, or drop the "same values" claim.
- situation (consistency): `src/nio/agents.py` line 12 is `TIERS = {"cheap", "strong", "max"}`, and card validation rejects any other tier. A card with `tier: frontier` fails validation today, so a task rated `Tier: frontier` and a card cannot share a value set until FR-17 lands. The spec does not say FR-15 depends on FR-17.
- fix: change FR-15 to "the same values agent cards use once FR-17 is in place", or note the dependency on FR-17.
- disposition: spec-fix by agent: FR-15: same values as agent cards once FR-17 adds frontier

### J-3 The word "tier" already names the jury's risk tier
- quote: "**Model tier**: cheap, strong, max or frontier"
- situation (consistency): `src/nio/records.py` line 34 gives verdict records a `tier` field with `low|medium|high`, and `src/nio/cli.py` line 75 names `--tier` "the ladder rung triage picked". D-261027-vi67 rejected low/medium/high partly because "the names clash with the jury's risk tier". The spec's `Tier:` line, the glossary, and the estimate table use "tier" for the model class, with no note on the existing jury meaning. A reader of `nio query` output could confuse a task's `Tier:` with a verdict's `tier`.
- situation (consistency): `src/nio/templates/verdict.md` line 11 defines `tier:` on verdict records as a jury risk level, `low | medium | high`, and `jury.py` line 37 defaults the ledger's `tier` to `"medium"`. An agent reading `tier` in memory or in a jury ledger may take it for a model tier, or the reverse. The glossary does not say the two are separate.
- fix: add one sentence to the Glossary that the jury's risk tier is a different field, or rename the task field.
- disposition: spec-fix by agent: Glossary: model tier is not the jury's risk tier field

### J-5 A justify-or-remove task must serve an AC and must not
- quote: "IF a task serves no AC THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL fail the check, naming the task."
- quote: "and count such a task as covering no AC"
- quote: "IF a task cites an AC, task or epic ID that the spec or `tasks.md` doesn't define THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL fail the check, naming the task and the ID."
- situation (logic): A task under `#### Fixes` has `From: J-4 (implementation-E-2, round 1)` and `Serves: J-4`. FR-49 and AC-51 say the check passes. FR-49 also says the task covers no AC, so FR-11 and AC-17 say it fails as "serving no AC". J-4 is also defined in neither the spec nor `tasks.md`, so FR-9 would fail it as an undefined ID. AC-51 is true only if FR-11 and FR-9 each get an unwritten exception.
- fix: Add the exception to FR-11 ("a `Fixes` task whose `Serves:` is a `J-n` its `From:` names is exempt") and to FR-9. Alternatively, make a justify-or-remove task cite an AC like any other task.
- validation: confirmed: FR-49 says a `J-n` task "counts as covering no AC", so FR-11 ("IF a task serves no AC THEN fail") and AC-17 still apply to it. FR-9 fails undefined IDs, and `J-4` is defined in neither the spec nor `tasks.md`. FR-49 and AC-51 give no exception to FR-11 or FR-9, so AC-51 can't pass as written.
- disposition: spec-fix by agent: FR-9 and FR-11 except a task FR-49 allows to serve a J-n finding

### J-6 The clash rule fails two parallel tasks that cannot run together
- quote: "IF two tasks marked parallel name the same file THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL fail the check, naming both tasks and the file."
- quote: "SHALL let a `Parallel: yes` task depend on other tasks, starting it only once they are done"
- quote: "decide whether a task runs in parallel only from its `Parallel:` and `Depends on:` lines"
- situation (logic): T-1 is `Parallel: yes` and names `src/a.py`. T-4 is `Parallel: yes`, has `Depends on: T-1`, and names `src/a.py`. FR-48 starts T-4 only after T-1 is done, so they never overlap. FR-13 and the first row of the clash table (yes, yes, shares a file) still fail the check with "parallel clash". FR-47 says `Depends on:` decides parallelism, but FR-13 and the table never use it. AC-50 and AC-27 list a task that has a dependency as "parallel", and the spec never says what "parallel" then means.
- fix: Say whether FR-13 exempts pairs where one task depends on the other, directly or through other tasks. Add that column to the clash table. State plainly what the estimate's "parallel" list means for a task with dependencies.
- validation: confirmed: FR-13 and the first row of the clash table fail any two `Parallel: yes` tasks that share a file. FR-48 lets a `Parallel: yes` task depend on others and start only after they are done, and FR-47 says `Depends on:` decides parallelism. Nothing exempts a dependent pair, so FR-13 contradicts FR-48 and AC-50, and "parallel" is left undefined for a dependent task.
- disposition: spec-fix by agent: FR-13 and the clash table exempt pairs where one depends on the other (follows FR-48); glossary defines parallel task

### J-7 AC-6 demands path checks the spec never requires and that new files would fail
- quote: "each path exists in the repo or sits in a directory that exists"
- situation (logic): No spec with no `plan.md` adds a new package, for example a task whose `Files:` is `src/nio/tasks/check.py` in a directory that does not exist yet. AC-6's observable says that task is wrong. FR-19 only says to name the files, and no FR makes `nio check tasks` verify paths. So the rule is either unenforced or rejects valid tasks that create new directories.

### J-8 FR-45 does not say which tasks count as dependents, or what a foundational task is
- quote: "fail the check when a foundational task cites an AC none of its dependent tasks serve"
- situation (logic): T-1 is foundational with `Serves: AC-1`. T-5 depends on T-1 and serves AC-2. T-8 depends on T-5 (so only indirectly on T-1) and serves AC-1. Read directly, the check fails T-1 for citing AC-1. Read as transitive, it passes. The check also has no stated way to tell a foundational epic from a story epic, since FR-46 bans epic-level dependency lines. Only the epic naming a user story separates them.
- fix: Say "directly depend" or "directly or transitively depend". Say how the check recognises the foundational epic, for example an epic naming no user story.
- disposition: spec-fix by agent: FR-45: dependents directly or through other tasks; foundational epic = the epic naming no user story

### J-10 Tests and requirements need the CLI state and implement stage that the non-goals exclude
- quote: "Building the CLI's state file and `nio flow` (#45) or the implement stage (#43)"

AC-36 needs a "green" state and a guard that refuses "done" without review, and AC-29 needs an implement stage that refuses to start. Neither exists in this spec, so the two acceptance criteria cannot be run as written. The human's intake says those belong to #45 and #43.
- fix: either move AC-36, AC-37 and the "claimed" wording in AC-30 to #45's spec, or state in the non-goal that this spec's ACs are checked on fixtures that model the state. Confirm which with the human.

AC-29 needs the implement stage to refuse to start, and FR-33 requires that behaviour. The spec doesn't say these ACs run on fixtures, and the non-goal says it only defines what "finished" means.

### J-15 The state table has undecidable cells, and FR-25 has one AC
- quote: "reject: #45 decides (DF-1)"
- quote: "when it is set to done without a review, then the change is refused"
- situation (testability): the cell "test fails (red)" in the `green` and `review` rows says only that #45 decides. A test of that transition cannot say whether to expect reject or pass. FR-25 lists a guarded path of seven steps with a reject for every wrong step. Only one skip-review case (AC-36) is tested. Rejecting `claimed → done`, a double claim, and pending claimed before its dependencies are done all go untested. An implementation that guards only the green-to-done step passes every AC.
- fix: add ACs for the other reject cells, or one AC per row family. Mark the DF-1 cells as out of scope for tests, as in the deferred section.
- validation: confirmed: The `green` and `review` rows have "reject: #45 decides (DF-1)" in the `test fails (red)` column, an open deferral that a test can't pin down. FR-25 lists seven guarded steps, but only AC-36 (green to done) tests a reject. Rejects such as claimed to done, double claim and claim before dependencies are done have no AC.
- disposition: spec-fix by agent: New AC-56, AC-57 for claimed-to-done, claim before dependencies, double claim; DF-1 cells stay deferred

### J-16 The decision-record AC cannot be triggered by a test
- quote: "Given the drafter chooses between two designs while writing tasks, when it is done, then the choice is recorded as a decision."
- situation (testability): whether the model chooses between designs is its own call. An e2e run on a fixture may never hit the Given. Then "one new decision record" cannot be asserted, or a decision is written when none was made. The test passes or fails by chance. Nothing says what counts as a design choice.
- fix: pin a fixture where two designs are forced, such as a spec that allows two storage options. Or move the check to the card's instruction, with the fixture's decision as the Observable.

### J-19 Fallback for an unmapped frontier tier differs from today's code
- quote: "a host with no frontier model uses its max model."
- situation (consistency): a task or card with `Tier: frontier` on a host with no frontier mapping. Today `src/nio/agents.py` `resolve()` returns no model for an unmapped tier, and `render` prints "WARN ... no model for tier ...; nio-<name> inherits the parent's". FR-17 says such a host uses its max model. The spec does not say whether the new rule replaces the inherit-and-warn rule for existing cards, so an implementer could go either way and AC-26 would not settle it.
- fix: state in FR-17 whether the max-model fallback replaces the current WARN-and-inherit behaviour, for `frontier` only or for every tier.

### J-20 AC-42 and AC-1 do not name a route, so on a full spec they contradict FR-2's plan-approval clause
- quote: "Given a spec whose jury the human closed with a reason, when the tasks stage starts, then it proceeds."
- quote: "For a full spec it SHALL also refuse until `nio check plan <slug> --approved` exits 0, and say the plan must be approved first."
- situation (logic): A full spec has its spec gate closed by the human with a reason, and its plan is not approved. AC-42 says the tasks stage proceeds with no refusal and starts the drafter. FR-2 and AC-59 say it refuses and writes no `tasks.md`. AC-1 has the same problem: "Given an approved spec with US-1 and US-2 and no shared setup" names no route, so on a full spec without an approved plan it cannot produce `tasks.md`.
- fix: Name the route in the Given of AC-42, AC-1 and AC-2, for example a bug-fix spec, or a full spec whose plan is approved. A fixture that is plainly one or the other would also do.
- validation: grounded: raised in a re-review below blocker: a note only
